title: Linked List Pointers: Reverse a Singly Linked List
oneLiner: Walk the list once with three pointers (prev, curr, next) and flip each node's Next to point backward.
keyTakeaway: Before you overwrite curr.Next, save it: next = curr.Next; curr.Next = prev; prev = curr; curr = next. When curr runs off the end, prev is the new head. Every linked list rewiring problem is this same discipline: never cut a link you still need to walk.
explanation:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse it and return the new head: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> null becomes 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> null. You could copy the values into an array and rebuild, but that costs O(n) extra space and skips the actual skill, which is rewiring pointers in place.

Keep two pointers: prev (the head of the part you have already reversed, starting as null) and curr (the next node to process, starting at head). At each node, do four things in this order. Save next = curr.Next, because the next line destroys it. Set curr.Next = prev, which flips this node to point backward. Move prev = curr, since curr is now the head of the reversed part. Move curr = next to continue down the part that hasn't been touched yet. When curr becomes null, every node has been flipped and prev points at the old tail, which is the new head.

At every moment the list is split into two separate chains: the reversed chain starting at prev, and the untouched chain starting at curr. Each step moves one node from the front of the second chain to the front of the first. Thinking of it that way makes the order of the four lines obvious, and it is the same mental model you need for harder variants: reversing only positions m to n, reversing in groups of k, or checking whether a list is a palindrome by reversing its second half.

A recursive version also works (reverse the rest, then set head.Next.Next = head and head.Next = null), but it uses O(n) call stack, so the iterative one is the version to know cold.

The visualization shows the original list with curr highlighted; "collected so far" is the reversed chain hanging off prev.

recognitionSignals: The problem asks you to reverse a linked list, or a piece of one (a range, every k nodes, the second half).
You must rearrange nodes in place with O(1) extra space, so copying values into an array isn't allowed.
A list needs to be read backward (palindrome check, adding numbers stored most significant digit first) and there are no Prev pointers.
gotchas: Save curr.Next before overwriting it; if you set curr.Next = prev first, the rest of the list is unreachable.
Return prev, not head or curr. After the loop curr is null and head is the new TAIL, whose Next is now null.
Start prev at null, not at head. Starting at head makes the old head point to itself and the result loops forever.
confusableWith: Linked Lists: Reverse a Doubly Linked List (Fundamentals) swaps two pointers per node and needs no separate prev variable, because each node already knows its predecessor. Here only Next exists, so you carry prev yourself.

Array Reversal: Two Pointers, One Pass (Fundamentals) swaps values from both ends inward. A singly linked list can't walk backward from the tail, so you reverse the links front to back instead of swapping values.

complexity.note: One pass, flipping each node's Next once; only the prev, curr and next pointers are stored. (The recursive version is also O(n) time but uses O(n) call stack.)

referenceSolutions.python:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr is not None:
        nxt = curr.next  # save it before the next line overwrites it
        curr.next = prev  # flip this node to point backward
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    return prev  # the old tail
